strengths: Long-horizon agentic coding and multi-step planning
Self-critique and iterative refinement when asked
weaknesses: Can over-explain — may produce more prose than needed without instruction
Higher cost per token; not the right pick for high-volume cheap calls
Tendency toward thoroughness can slow latency-sensitive flows
prompting_quirks: Responds particularly well to XML tags for structured input (e.g. <document>, <instructions>)
Asking for chain-of-thought explicitly improves hard-reasoning tasks
Performs best when given an explicit role and acceptance criteria
Will push back honestly if asked; treat it as a colleague, not a yes-man
best_for: Architecture decisions and system design reviews
Agentic coding (Claude Code) — multi-file refactors, debugging at scale
Tasks where being wrong has high cost
avoid_for: Bulk classification or simple extraction (use Haiku or a smaller model)
Single-line completions where a fast cheap model suffices
notes: The frontier model in the Claude 4 family. Treat it as a senior collaborator: it benefits from context, planning, and pushback, and is worth waiting for on hard problems.
pricing_notes: Standard rate. Prompt caching can reduce input cost ~90% on cached content; batch API ~50% off. Verify before using for budget planning.
